newsitem.title: USA: Asthma sufferers may overuse inhalers - U.S. study.
newsitem.headline: Asthma sufferers may overuse inhalers - U.S. study.

text.p: People with mild asthma may not need regular treatment with an inhaler, according to a new U.S. study which suggests that using it when symptoms occur may be just as effective.

For many years doctors believed that regularly inhaling the anti-asthma medicine albuterol was more effective than "as-needed" treatment for the four percent of the U.S. population that suffers from mild asthma. But other studies have questioned that notion.

New research from a group led by Dr. Jeffrey M. Drazen of Brigham and Women's Hospital and published in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine was an effort to assess the two treatments in a large group of patients.

The researchers found that 126 people who regularly inhaled albuterol four times a day remained just as healthy as 129 volunteers who only took the medicine when they needed it, even though they only consumed one-sixth as much medication.
People who regularly inhaled albuterol showed no side effects and there was no evidence that the effectiveness of the drug waned in any of the volunteers during the 16 weeks of the study.
Albuterol is made by several manufacturers.
